newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Edegel plans new generators.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Edegel plans new generators.

text.p: Utility Edegel has medium-term plans with miner Morococha to build four hydroelectric generators throughout Peru for a total investment of $300 million, its general manager said.
Pablo Errazuriz told Reuters that Edegel, recently added to the Lima Stock Exchange's blue-chip index, was also planning a $90 million hydro-electric generator in the highland locality of Canchis.
The most advanced project was with Morococha for a $60 million, 40-megawatt hydro-electric station in Yanango, near the central Andean town of Tarma, he said.
"In this project, the investment will be divided between Edegel and Morococha 50 percent each," said Errazuriz, adding that a feasibility study would be completed by the end of 1997.
This and the other projects with Morococha would create an extra 200 megawatts' generating potential, while the Canchis generator would add a further 60 megawatts.

"We have received from the government a temporary concession to study electricity generation using the resources of the Canchis river, 70 kilometers east of Lima," he said. "The concession is for two years."
Edegel, privatized in 1995, has an installed capacity of 700 megawatts and supplies distributors Edelnor, Luz del Sur and others.
The company is controlled by a consortium consisting of U.S. company Entergy Corp, Chile's Endesa and local companies Grana y Montero and Banco Wiese.
Peru has one of the lowest levels of energy consumption in Latin America and is regarded by analysts and investors as having enormous potential for growth in the medium-term.
According to the government, per capita electricity consumption in Peru is merely 550 kilowatt hours per year, compared to a regional average of 1,166 kilowatt hours annually.
